request:
Simplify managed PR publication

## Problem

`publish_pr` currently contains its own reconciliation protocol around a GitWeave-managed Pull Request branch.

It:

- searches for an existing managed PR
- reads the remote branch with `ls-remote`
- compares it with in-memory expected state
- rejects unexpected remote state
- pushes with an exact lease
- preserves additional in-process state so retries can recognize a push that may already have succeeded

This is similar to the speculative synchronization complexity tracked for existing-PR `sync_pr` in #38.

Because GitWeave itself owns the managed branch namespace, publication can remain much simpler.

## Expected outcome

Reduce `publish_pr` to the minimum needed to publish the selected artifact and create/update the corresponding PR.

Conceptually:

```text
selected artifact
  ↓
push managed branch
  ↓
create or update PR
```

Use ordinary Git behavior and the smallest necessary lease/update semantics for updating an existing managed branch.

Remove extra remote-state reconciliation and special retry-success recognition unless a concrete observed failure demonstrates that they are needed.

GitHub should remain authoritative for PR creation/edit failures.

## Context

The guiding principle is:

> Do not build a second synchronization protocol around an operation Git and GitHub already implement.

This issue applies the same simplification direction as #38 to GitWeave-managed PR publication.


User directive: GitWeave implements, creates a separate PR, reviews/fixes iteratively and merges only when clean. Stop on unsupported operations or permission/allowance limits and ask the user. No parent manual substitute is authorized.
